content.title: About
content.content: Frozen, unprepared carrots are whole carrot roots that have been peeled and flash‑frozen shortly after harvest. They retain their natural sweet flavor, bright orange color, and most of their nutrients.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Carrots are one of the most widely cultivated vegetables, grown in over 100 countries.
Freezing within 24 hours of harvest preserves up to 90 % of vitamin C.
The orange hue comes from high levels of beta‑carotene, a provitamin A.
Frozen carrots can be added directly to soups, stews, and stir‑fries without thawing.
In the United States, carrots rank among the top five most consumed frozen vegetables.

items.title: Rich in beta‑carotene
items.content: Beta‑carotene is converted to vitamin A in the body, supporting vision, immunity, and skin health.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Carrots provide vitamin C, vitamin E, and polyphenols that help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Dietary fiber promotes regular bowel movements and contributes to a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: 100 g of carrots contain about 35 kcal, making them a great choice for calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potassium aids fluid balance and helps maintain normal blood pressure.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: A small number of individuals may experience an allergic reaction to carrots.

items.title: Nitrate content
items.content: Like many root vegetables, carrots can accumulate nitrates; it is advisable not to store them excessively long.

items.title: Texture loss with prolonged storage
items.content: Extended freezing can make carrots softer after thawing, limiting their use in raw preparations.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Add frozen carrots directly to boiling soups, stews, sauces, or stir‑fries. For a softer texture, briefly thaw them in the microwave or under running water before cooking.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep carrots in an airtight bag at –18 °C or lower. Once opened, use within 6‑8 months. Do not thaw and refreeze.
